department: Department of Physics, Applied Physics and Astronomy

deadline.value: Applications for full consideration are due January 15 (the page gives no year, so the Fall 2027 cycle is assumed).
deadline.quote: For full consideration, applications must be submitted by Jan. 15.

gre_general.quote: Note: GRE is optional. The minimum required TOEFL score is 80

gre_subject.value: The physics pages do not mention the Physics GRE Subject test.

toefl_min.value: The physics page gives an iBT minimum of 80; the graduate school now uses a 0-6 scale with a minimum of 4 for new test takers.
toefl_min.quote: The minimum required TOEFL score is 80

also.quote: Binghamton University requires a minimum TOEFL score of 4, with no band below 4.

fee_waiver.value: The department waives the application fee for a limited number of qualified PhD candidates who request it by January 1.
fee_waiver.quote: We are able to waive the application fee for a limited number of qualified PhD candidates who submit a request by Jan. 1.

supervisor.value: The physics pages do not say whether a faculty supervisor must agree before admission.

funding.value: PhD candidates are funded through teaching assistantships, research assistantships, and fellowships including stipend and tuition.
funding.quote: PhD candidates are funded through teaching assistantships, research assistantships, and fellowships, which include a stipend, tuition and health insurance. MS candidates are self-funded.

entry_route.value: The department welcomes applicants with an undergraduate degree in physics or a closely related field.
entry_route.quote: We welcome applications from students who have successfully completed an undergraduate degree in physics or closely related fields.

notes: The physics TOEFL minimum of 80 is the pre-2026 iBT scale and differs from the graduate school's 0-6 scale (4); both are kept. The catalog table (GRE Not required; Fall January 15) is not quoted because table cells are not usable. Fee waiver request date Jan. 1 has no year; the 2026/27 cycle is assumed.
